title: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
summary: Starship Test Flight 15 marked the first time Elon Musk's company tried to catch both the booster and upper stage of the rocket.
text:
After a booster explosion on Friday, SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage, or spacecraft, portion of its massive Starship rocket from orbit on Saturday — a triumphant milestone for the company.
SpaceX made the historic catch using its "chopsticks," mechanical arms attached to a launch tower, at its facility in Starbase, Texas.
Test Flight 15, the most ambitious Starship test yet, marked the first time Musk's company attempted to catch both the rocket's booster and upper stage.
During the first phase of the test flight on Friday, SpaceX failed to catch and recover the booster, instead diverting it to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico where it exploded before hitting the water.
The rocket's upper stage then continued into orbit and flew around the Earth 14 times before successfully landing on SpaceX's launch tower, nicknamed Mechazilla.
The Hawaii Department of Transportation issued a temporary pause on some West Coast flights Friday, due to debris risk from the flight.
ai_summary: SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms at its Texas facility following a test flight.

text:
The 2030 World Cup final will be in Spain, Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) head Rafael Louzan reiterated on Saturday, adding that he is not considering “withdrawing” should he be wrong.
Spain is organising the next World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. The decision on the venue for the final will be made in 2028, Louzan said.
Spain favours Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium for the final. Portugal does not have a suitable stadium but Morocco has suggested the 115,000-capacity Hassan II Stadium being built in Benslimane near Casablanca.
“There is no other plan than for the final to be held in Spain,” said Louzan at a conference at the RFEF’s Ciudad del Futbol on the outskirts of Madrid.
“I am not currently considering the possibility of withdrawing from Spain, as the prospect of Spain not hosting the final is not on the table,” he said.
Louzan was responding to Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the right-wing People’s Party.

summary: STARBASE, Texas, Nov 14 - SpaceX's next-generation Starship spacecraft cruised around the globe on Saturday nearing the end of its 15th test flight and what the company hoped would be an unprecedented pinpoint return landing at the exact spot in Texas from which it launched.
text:
SpaceX's Starship nears end of 15th test flight and return-landing attempt
STARBASE, Texas, Nov 14 - SpaceX's next-generation Starship spacecraft cruised around the globe on Saturday nearing the end of its 15th test flight and what the company hoped would be an unprecedented pinpoint return landing at the exact spot in Texas from which it launched.
Starship's uncrewed upper stage is poised to re-enter Earth's atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and steer back toward its launch tower, then make an engine-controlled final descent into the embrace of giant mechanical arms designed to catch the vehicle as it hovers over the launchpad.
If successful, it will mark the first round-trip voyage of a vertically launched spacecraft to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, achieving a key test of Elon Musk's long-pursued goal of producing a fully reusable rocket system.

text:
The UK Health Security Agency has issued a yellow cold-health alert for three regions of England, warning that falling temperatures could pose health risks to elderly people and those with underlying medical conditions.
The alert covers the North West of England, North East of England, and Yorkshire and the Humber, and will run from 9pm on Sunday, November 15, until 9am on Thursday, November 19.
The agency disclosed this in an update published on Saturday, as part of its cold-health alerts for the 2026/2027 winter season.
It said other regions of England were currently unaffected by the alert.
According to the UKHSA, yellow cold-health alerts may be issued during periods of cold or heat that are unlikely to affect most people but could have an impact on particularly vulnerable groups.

As refugees continued to pour into Pakistan, often surviving unspeakable violence en route, Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, in a true display of leadership, met with the frazzled masses, urging them to keep hope alive. This, along with the busting of an RSS cell in Karachi, and a violent mob attack on Dawn’s Delhi press, marked some of the prominent stories from Sept 15 to 21, 1947.
Soothing words
Many among the millions that had crossed over into Pakistan at the time of Independence had literally been through hell. They had witnessed murder, arson and communal frenzy on their way to what was supposed to be the promised land. In such delicate times, leaders are supposed to put aside protocol and mingle with the masses in order to empathise with them. The Quaid did just that, as a news report from the Sept 18 issue shows.

Nearly 10,000 more cancer patients in England will not be treated on time because the government will fail to meet its targets, amid a failure of leadership, focus and resource, experts have warned.
The NHS set an interim target to treat 80% of cancer patients within 62 days of urgent referral or consultant upgrade by March 2027. But with little more than 100 days to go, the proportion of patients starting treatment on time in September was 70.7%, down from 71.9% in August, NHS figures show.

SANTIAGO, Chile — Chile's ultraconservative president finds himself on the back foot after just eight months in power.
José Antonio Kast, a politician who spent a career railing against progressive issues, reproductive rights and welfare policies from the extreme fringes of right-wing politics, now finds himself with just 24% approval in the polls.
It is less than a year since Kast stormed to the presidency in December 2025 by avoiding all mention of his hardline stances on social matters, focusing instead on two hot-button issues whipped up in the national media: illegal immigration and public security.

title: The death of the night out? How Mexico City’s youth are socializing
summary: Young people are increasingly turning away from boozy nights out. So what are they doing instead? MND contributor Marta Delgado explains. The post The death of the night out? How Mexico City’s youth are socializing appeared first on Mexico News Daily
text:
What if the problem isn’t that young people have stopped going out, but that we’ve been getting the night out wrong all along?
For decades, the formula seemed pretty straightforward: Friday night meant getting dressed up, meeting friends, drinking too much, dancing until the early hours and spending Saturday recovering. Going out was practically a weekend obligation.
But for a growing number of young people, getting wasted is losing its appeal. And the traditional clubbing experience is no longer the default way to socialize.
Instead, think dinner with friends, a long walk, a fitness class, a coffee that turns into a three-hour conversation, or a night at someone’s apartment. Alcohol hasn’t disappeared, and neither has the desire to have fun. But the priorities seem to be shifting.
So, is the night out dying? Or are we simply learning to have a good time differently? In Mexico City, where nightlife has long been part of the city’s appeal, I wanted to find out.
Is Gen Z drinking less?

text:
The United States was slow to embrace offshore wind, with its first small-scale commercial wind farm coming online in 2016. It would take another eight years before the country launched its first utility-scale offshore wind project in 2024. While many other countries around the globe were rapidly developing offshore wind projects as part of energy diversification strategies, the United States mainly pursued solar photovoltaics and onshore wind projects.
The United States has significant potential to develop its offshore wind capacity, but it has only just begun to construct commercial offshore wind projects. According to the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), the United States has over 4,000 GW of technical resource potential, or 13,500 terawatt-hours (TWh) of generation per year in federal waters and the Great Lakes. text:
The Amazon rainforest has revealed two more of its biological secrets, with scientists identifying two previously unrecognised species of howler monkeys through groundbreaking genetic research. The discovery adds to the known biodiversity of the world's largest tropical rainforest, while raising concerns about the survival of these primates as deforestation continues to destroy their habitats.
The study, led by researchers from the University of Salford and international collaborators, analysed the genomes of 11 howler monkey species found across South and Central America. The research identified two distinct species, Alouatta iroi and Alouatta matogrossensis, which were previously classified within other known species.
Published in Communications Biology, the findings offer a more detailed understanding of how howler monkeys evolved, how their populations are distributed and why the Amazon Basin is home to such remarkable primate diversity.

title: NASA’s Voyager 1 to hit new space distance record of one light-day
summary: The probe was launched in 1977 but it continues to relay space-related data back to a team of NASA scientists daily.
text:
NASA’s Voyager 1 to hit new space distance record of one light-day
The probe was launched in 1977 but it continues to relay space-related data back to a team of NASA scientists daily.
NASA has announced that its Voyager 1 probe will soon become humanity’s first object to travel one light-day from Earth.
On Wednesday, the robotic space probe will hit the milestone of travelling at least 16 billion miles since its launch in 1977, a distance equal to one light-day, or how far light can travel in 24 hours.
The probe completed its Saturn flyby in 1980, the end of its primary planetary mission, and is currently travelling at roughly 36,000 miles per hour (58km/h) in interstellar space, the vast gap between stars.
NASA expects it to take 18,000 years to travel a full light-year, and double that before it nears another star.
Plutonium-powered Voyager 1 was launched shortly before another probe, Voyager 2. Both continue to relay data back to Earth daily, including readings on the strength and d
ai_summary: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is set to become the first human-made object to travel one light-day from Earth.

title: Awujale Succession: Why govt can’t abdicate its statutory responsibility, By Soji Adeyemi
summary: Government must not usurp customary authority. But neither must it surrender its statutory responsibility in the name of avoiding controversy. The post Awujale Succession: Why govt can’t abdicate its statutory responsibility, By Soji Adeyemi appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
text:
The controversy surrounding the succession to the revered Awujale throne of Ijebuland has reached a point where the distinction between legitimate customary authority and the statutory responsibilities of government must be clearly understood. What should ordinarily be a structured process governed by tradition, established chieftaincy procedures and the laws of Ogun State is increasingly being complicated by misinformation, political insinuations and attempts to portray legitimate government oversight as interference.
At the heart of the controversy is a fundamental question: Should the Ogun State Government abandon its statutory responsibilities simply because the succession involves a traditional institution?
The answer is unequivocally no.
The Awujale stool is not an ordinary traditional institution. It is one of the most distinguished and historically significant traditional thrones in Yorubaland. Its integrity, prestige and continuity are matters of considerable public interest.
ai_summary: This opinion piece argues that the Ogun State government must maintain its statutory oversight role in the traditional succession process of the Awujale throne.

The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said.
Signalling a sharp rise in mortgage payments for an estimated 2.3 million homeowners who will have to refinance their loans next year, Huw Pill said that while the decision to nudge interest rates from 3.75% to 4% earlier this month was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, “we have further to go”.
Pill told the Financial Times: “My view would be, we will see evidence that motivates further rises,” adding that the central bank would “do what is necessary to get inflation back to 2% through time”.

Across Central America’s so-called Dry Corridor, farming families live at the mercy of the rains. In southwestern Honduras, Anastacio Martínez Gómez has spent most of his 73 years learning to work the land. But experience can only take him so far.
"When there’s no water, that’s where you run out of ideas,” he says.
In his village of Palagua, dry seasons can last five or six months. For years, a failed maize or bean harvest meant searching for work elsewhere.
Then, Mr. Martínez volunteered part of his land for a reservoir – opening up new possibilities for his whole community.
The Dry Corridor is a drought-prone region stretching across parts of Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua, where more than seven million people do not have guaranteed access to food.

text:
On September 27, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy posted a video on X with the words “GAME CHANGER.” “Introducing ‘SMART’—the new air traffic management tool that saves YOU time, cuts back DELAYS, and makes your flying experience BETTER,” he wrote. This was a new AI-infused air traffic control system. Almost three weeks later, that post would get a new life, as a nervous joke, as the FAA issued a national groundstop on Friday the 13th that instantly threw the world’s airline schedules into chaos. title: Mohamed Salah settles debate on surpassing Hossam Hassan
summary: Mohamed Salah settles debate on surpassing Hossam Hassan Egypt Independent
text:
Mohamed Salah, the star of the Egyptian national team, has put an end to the ongoing debate regarding his status as the all-time leading goalscorer for the national team.
Salah scored two goals during Egypt’s match against Malawi on Friday, as part of the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.
The situation sparked a debate on social media platforms as to whether Salah had surpassed Hossam Hassan’s record as the top scorer for the Egyptian national team.
While some say Salah has reached his 70th goal, surpassing Hassan (who scored 69), others argue that two of Salah’s goals were not officially counted; according to this latter view, Salah currently has 68 goals, not 70.
Salah posted an image on his social media accounts featuring the number 70, marking his status as a historic top scorer for the Egyptian national team.
ai_summary: Mohamed Salah confirmed his status as the all-time leading goalscorer for the Egyptian national football team following a debate over official statistics.

To perform NRP, doctors attach an external pump to a donor minutes after their circulation has ended and they've been declared dead. The pump restores blood flow to their hearts, lungs, kidneys, liver and other organs to keep them from deteriorating.

title: Fifteen taken to hospital after deliberate fire at Glasgow flats
summary: The four-storey building on Copland Street in Ibrox was evacuated after the blaze broke out on Friday afternoon.
text:
Fifteen taken to hospital after deliberate fire at Glasgow flats
- Published
Police are treating a fire at a block of flats in Glasgow as deliberate.
Four fire engines were sent to the four-storey building on Copland Road, in the Ibrox area, just after 17:00 on Friday after reports of a fire on the ground floor.
Firefighters and paramedics initially said they were dealing with "multiple casualties" and police have now confirmed 15 people were taken to hospital as a precaution.
The fire was extinguished and crews left the scene by 22:00.
A section of Paisley Road West was closed while fire crews tackled the blaze.
One image from the scene showed a firefighter up a ladder while at least two residents looked out from a first floor window.
A Police Scotland spokesperson said the building was evacuated and added: "The fire is being treated as wilful and inquiries are ongoing."
ai_summary: Fifteen people were hospitalized following a deliberate fire at a block of flats in Glasgow.

text:
South Sudan, the world’s newest country, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) postponed its first national elections from December to February amid growing ethnic and political battles.
The legislative and presidential elections had been scheduled for December 22, after already being delayed several times. The United Nations had warned that a vote could set off widespread conflict.
The electoral commission issued a new calendar on social media, giving a new voting date of February 11, with results to be announced four days later.
Commission secretary general Ahon Malou Lueth confirmed the change to AFP but would not give a reason or other details.
President Salva Kiir’s government forces and followers of detained former Vice President Riek Machar have been involved in escalating, deadly confrontations in recent months.
Other ethnic tensions and cattle-rustling battles have also complicated the picture in one of the world’s poorest countries.
South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011

There are books that one reads only once, and there are books that one returns to at regular intervals. Of this quartet, the last is surely the least known, which is one reason for me to write about it here. A second, and perhaps more compelling, reason is that this column is being published on Jawaharlal Nehru’s 137th birth anniversary.

title: OSCE may fail to agree on 2027 chairmanship — Russian envoy
summary: Some countries are engaged in nonstop shuttle diplomacy in search of a solution, Dmitry Polyansky said
text:
VIENNA, November 14. /TASS/. Member states of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) are actively holding diplomatic consultations on which country will chair the organization in 2027, but they may fail to reach consensus, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE Dmitry Polyansky told TASS.
"I expect we’ll find some way forward. But we can’t rule out that possibility entirely," he said when asked whether the talks could end without an agreement. In that event, OSCE Secretary General Feridun Sinirlioglu would most likely oversee the organization’s work for a time, though that would require further decisions. "The OSCE is a fairly resilient organization, so I think it will find a way forward even in that scenario," the diplomat noted.

text:
As smog hangs over Lahore, Pakistan's new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires
By Mubasher Bukhari
LAHORE, Nov 14 (Reuters) - As smog again settles over large parts of South Asia, Pakistani authorities are widening a crackdown on illegal stubble burning they say is fuelling the region's annual pollution crisis.
On Thursday, officers of a new quick-response unit swung off their vehicles at a paddy field on the edge of Lahore. Smoke curled low over the stubble, and the crew had the fire under control within minutes, keeping it fromadding to the haze over a city that Swiss group IQAir rated “very unhealthy” earlier this week.
Farmers in the regioncommonly set leftover rice residue alight after the October harvest, fuelling a toxic mix of industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust and construction dust that lingers under cold winter air, driving pollution to hazardous levels.

Egypt plans to set up a company under the Future of Egypt Authority to licence artisanal gold miners and free those jailed for illegal mining, after a meeting convened by tribal leader and business mogul Ibrahim al-Organi, a lawmaker said.
Mona Shaker, a National Front party lawmaker for Aswan, said in a Facebook video that people arrested while prospecting would be freed, but not anyone found to be involved in killings or drug offences.
The military has said it detained 151 Egyptians and 540 foreigners in its crackdown on illegal mining since June. It was not clear how many remain in custody or whether foreigners would be covered.
Pro-government media reported that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi directed the meeting, but no official statement has been issued.

text:
«التعليم العالي» تطلق حلقة جديدة من سلسلة «خطوة لقدام» حول مهارات التعامل مع النقد
تواصل الإدارة العامة للمكتب الإعلامي بوزارة التعليم العالي والبحث العلمي، تقديم حلقات سلسلة «خطوة لقدام» تحت شعار «طوّر نفسك.. طوّر مهاراتك»، والتي تستهدف تنمية مهارات الشباب الجامعي، ومساعدتهم على تطوير قدراتهم في مختلف جوانب الحياة.
وتتناول الحلقة مهارة «التعامل مع النقد»، من خلال توجيه الطلاب إلى الاستماع للنقد وفهم مضمونه قبل الرد عليه، والتمييز بين الملاحظات البناءة التي يمكن الاستفادة منها لتطوير الأداء، والكلام الذي يهدف إلى التجريح، مع عدم السماح للانتقادات السلبية بالتأثير على تقديرهم لذواتهم أو ثقتهم بقدراتهم.
وأكد الدكتور عادل عبدالغفار، المستشار الإعلامي والمتحدث الرسمي للوزارة، أهمية تنمية قدرة الطلاب على التعامل الواعي مع النقد، والاستفادة من الملاحظات التي تسهم في تحسين أدائهم وتطوير مهاراتهم، مع التمييز بين النقد الموضوعي والتجريح الشخصي، بما يساعدهم على بناء الثقة بالنفس، وتقبّل وجهات النظر المختلفة، ومواصلة السعي نحو تحقيق أهدافهم.
وتقدم السلسلة محتوى توعويًا مبسطًا من خلال الإنفوجرافات

Democrat Mary Peltola substantially grew her lead in Alaska’s U.S. Senate race, as she remained on track to unseat Republican incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan.
The Alaska Division of Elections counted more than 20,000 ballots Friday, bringing the total number of tallied ballots to over 279,000.
Peltola had 49.8% of first-choice votes counted as of Friday. Sullivan, the incumbent, had 46.1%.
“Alaskans have spoken, and it is clear that in the coming days Mary Peltola will be officially elected as their next United States Senator,” said Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, in a prepared statement.
The Division of Elections is set to continue counting ballots through Wednesday, the last day to accept absentee ballots mailed from overseas. Thousands of votes remain to be tallied.

text:
Demolition Day: This Cheshire farmhouse will be knocked down tomorrow after planners ruled it had been built illegally on green belt land
A charming farmhouse is set to be knocked down after it had been built illegally on green belt land.
The property on Dones View Farm in Dutton in Cheshire, will be demolished tomorrow at a cost of £20,000 after planners ruled he did not seek permission.
The home was constructed by retired builder Barry Devine, who bought it in 2000 and spent 19 years transforming the 19th-century barn into a sprawling house with separate wings.

YEREVAN, November 14. /TASS/. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan plans to visit Russia three times in December, he said at the Institute of International and European Affairs in Dublin.
"I’ll be in Russia three times in December. I’ll make three visits for talks. I’ll go to Russia for talks on December 3, 11 and 22. I hope we can maintain a friendly atmosphere in our relations with Russia," Pashinyan said.

text:
Airport-style passport and fingerprinting controls are to be introduced at Eurotunnel in an attempt to prevent “short-term and long-term chaos” in Folkestone and Calais.
In a breakthrough for travellers, the European Commission has agreed to a new system in which an “eagle eye” camera system, already used in Rome and Paris airports to supervise fingerprinting and facial imaging, will be used at the border between the UK and France.
Yann Leriche, the chief executive of Getlink, the Eurotunnel owner, said it had tried to replicate the “airport experience” but wanted to go much further.
Instead of getting out of the car and getting biometrics taken at a terminal building, holidaymakers and business travellers will now be greeted with special drive-through terminals in Folkestone and Calais.
Both sides are now equipped with 120 kiosks under the case of an eagle-eye camera that will be monitored by police, similar to e-gates at airports where police are not physically present at each gate.
ai_summary: The UK and EU have agreed to implement airport-style biometric border controls at the Eurotunnel to streamline travel and prevent congestion.

In South African family-law reform, we have had a very long season of waiting.
A time to investigate. A time to consult. A time to draft. Then another election, another administration and another legislative programme. For Parliament, a time to begin again. For families still waiting for protection, another time to weep. Again.
The South African Law Reform Commissionâs recently published report on a Single Marriage Statute (3 November 2026) offers an opportunity to change that refrain. Its proposed Protected Relationships Bill reaches beyond conventional marriage to recognise religious marriages and life partnerships in which the parties have undertaken reciprocal duties of support.

title: Section 27 and the overlooked crisis — why healthcare access starts with diabetes action
summary: Political acknowledgement must be backed by actionable public health measures, including early diagnosis, accessible primary healthcare screening, and uninterrupted medication supplies, if South Africa is to beat the country’s leading cause of natural death.
text:
This year marks three decades since South Africa adopted a Constitution rooted in human dignity, equality, and social justice. Enshrined within Section 27 is a promise: that every person in our country has the right to have access to healthcare services.
Yet, as we mark Diabetes Awareness Month this November, we are confronted by a sobering disconnect between constitutional ideals and lived reality.
The latest mortality figures from Statistics South Africa tell an unambiguous story. For three consecutive years, diabetes has stood as the leading recorded underlying natural cause of death in South Africa. In 2024, it accounted for more than 6% of all recorded deaths in the country. Every day, nearly 80 South Africans lose their lives to diabetes.

text:
The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.
“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.”

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?”

text:
Could one daily pill narrow the diabetes treatment gap in the Global South?
Globally, one in nine people lives with diabetes, as blockbuster injectable drugs begin making way for tablets instead.
Medication that has been a lifeline for patients with uncontrollable diabetes is now slowly shifting from injections to pills, a move that could fundamentally alter treatment for the disease – and who can access it.
This shift could also affect the treatment of obesity, a long misunderstood condition once associated with overeating and laziness, rather than the metabolic disorder it is now recognised as.
GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists therapy isn’t new. The first FDA-approved drug, Exenatide, hit the market in 2005 and was followed by Liraglutide in 2009, which was seen as a revolutionary alternative to insulin.

ai_summary: The shift from injectable diabetes medications to daily pills could significantly improve treatment accessibility and affordability for patients in the Global South.

Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state representative from the small island community of Sitka, won the race for Alaska governor, according to a race call by the Associated Press. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in state history.
Kreiss-Tomkins will replace outgoing Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a term-limited Republican who has been governor since 2018. The state's last Democratic governor was Tony Knowles, who left office in 2002.

text:
Alaskans have decided to stick with ranked choice voting, rejecting a ballot measure that sought to repeal the system, NBC News projects.
The unusual voting method was in the spotlight after a controversy around a potential spoiler candidate in the state’s competitive Senate race gathered steam in the final stretch of the election.
In Alaska, candidates from all parties run on the same primary ballot, with the top four vote-getters advancing to the general election. Voters then rank those candidates in order of preference, and if no one eclipses the 50% threshold on the first ballot, the race goes to ranked choice tabulation.
The fourth-place finisher is eliminated, and their supporters are redistributed based on how voters ranked the other candidates on the ballot. The process continues until a candidate reaches a majority.

title: German spies granted sweeping new powers
summary: Parliament passes legislation months after a thwarted attack at Leipzig-Halle airport, which Berlin linked to Russia.
text:
German spies granted sweeping new powers
The controversial bill comes just months after a thwarted attack at Leipzig-Halle airport which Berlin linked to Russia.
Germany’s parliament has approved sweeping new powers for the country’s intelligence agencies, allowing them to hack and disrupt adversaries under specified conditions as the government seeks to counter espionage and cyberattacks.
The Bundestag passed the legislation on Friday by 308 votes to 190, with 71 abstentions. The governing Christian Democrats and Social Democrats backed the reform, while the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and Die Linke, or the Left Party, opposed it.
The changes expand the role of Germany’s foreign intelligence agency, the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND), and its domestic intelligence service, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV), beyond gathering and analysing information to actively disrupting certain threats.

summary: Commercial merchant ships continue to avoid the ports of Odessa, Chernomorsk, and Yuzhny
text:
MOSCOW, November 14. /TASS/. Ukraine has lost over $7 billion in foreign exchange revenue due to the nearly four-month-long shutdown of the Odessa Region ports, according to TASS calculations.
Commercial merchant ships continue to avoid the ports of Odessa, Chernomorsk, and Yuzhny. Only vessels affiliated with the Ukrainian armed forces are calling at those ports. Meanwhile, maritime trade is being routed through the Danube ports of Izmail in Ukraine and Constanta in Romania, which together can handle no more than one-third of the exports that previously passed through the Odessa Region ports. Consequently, Ukraine exported only about half of its planned agricultural exports in October. Exports of metallurgical products ceased entirely at the end of September due to the shutdown of steel mills. These products together accounted for approximately 65% of Ukraine’s total exports and $26 billion in foreign exchange earnings per year.

summary: Enthusiastic crowds attended the games in Senegal, with China taking home the most gold medals. It's the first Olympic Games since Russia's war on Ukraine where Russian athletes can compete under their own flag.
text:
Senegal Youth Olympics in Dakar end on high note
November 14, 2026
The Senegal Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar ended Friday after two weeks of games on a high note.
It's the first time an African country has hosted an Olympic event, and African nations also brought home a record haul of medals. The Games were met with enthusiasm, with Dakar's streets and beaches filled with sports fans.
Nearly 2,700 young athletes took part in the games, which featured 153 medal events across 25 sports.
IOC president on Senegal games: 'Expectations have been exceeded'
"There is a beautiful African proverb, 'It take a village to raise a child.' And if these Youth Olympic Games have shown us anything it is what can happen when an entire country comes together for its young people," International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry said in a thank-you ceremony on Friday.

ai_summary: The Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, concluded successfully, marking the first time an African nation has hosted an Olympic event.

تستكمل محكمة جنايات مستأنف القاهرة، اليوم السبت، نظر استئناف متهم على حكم أول درجة الصادر بمعاقبته بالسجن المؤبد، لاتهامه لاشتراك مع آخرين في استعراض القوة والتلويح بالعنف وقتل صاحب مرسى والشروع فى قتل شقيقه بسبب خلافات سابقة ورغبته فى الثأر، بمنطقة قصر النيل.
وكانت النيابة العامة، أحالت المتهم إلى محكمة الجنايات لاتهامه بالاشتراك مع آخرين محكوم عليهما بقتل المجنى عليه «م. ص»، والشروع فى قتل شقيقه المجنى عليه «ر.ص» عمدا مع سبق الإصرار.
وكشفت التحريات، عن نشوب مشاجرة قبل الواقعة بأيام، اعتدى فيها المجنى عليه الأول على المتهم بحضور المجنى عليه الثانى، ما أوغر صدره، فعقد العزم على الانتقام منهما، وإزهاق روحيهما، واتفق مع المتهم الثانى «شقيقه»، والثالث «صديقه»، وآخرين مجهولين على ذلك، ففكروا ودبروا ووضعوا خطة قسموا فيها الأدوار، وفى اليوم المتفق عليه توجهوا إلى مسرح الحادث مستقلين حافلة ودراجتين ناريتين، ومدججين بأسلحة بيضاء «سنج، شوم، سكاكين، سيوف»، وما إن ظفروا بالمجنى عليهما حتى اعتدوا عليهما ضربا

US loses measles-free status after continued spread of the disease: Report
The reported decision by the Americas branch of the World Health Organization comes as the US battles the highest number of measles cases it has seen in more than three decades.
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has revoked the United States' measles-elimination status, ending a 26-year run after determining the country failed to halt continuous transmission of the highly contagious virus for more than a year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday (Nov 13).
The international health body did not immediately respond to a request from Reuters for comment on the report, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Social media users condemned the conductor’s behaviour and demanded action against him, as well as the transport company – Faisal Movers Group.

summary: Salah Becomes Egypt's All-Time Leading Scorer with 70 Goals news.sbs.co.kr
text:
▲ Egypt's Mohamed Salah 
  
African football legend Mohamed Salah has become the all-time leading goalscorer for the Egyptian national football team.
Playing in a Group B match of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Malawi held in Cairo, Egypt, Salah scored two goals late in the match to lead Egypt to a 5-0 victory.
Salah, who started the match, scored his goals in the closing stages.
He scored the team's fourth goal with a header in the 39th minute of the second half, and added the decisive goal from the penalty spot in the 5th minute of stoppage time.
With these goals, Salah brought his total to 70 in A-matches, surpassing Hossam Hassan (69 goals) to set a new record for the most goals in Egypt national team history.
Newly appointed manager Ali Maher marked his debut with a resounding victory, sending Egypt to the top of Group B.
The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be co-hosted by three countries—Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda—running from June 19 to July 17 next year.

A cruise ship with 129 people on board started sinking into the Mississippi River on Friday after being struck by a tanker.
American Cruise Lines’ paddle-wheel pleasure boat, American Heritage, was docked in New Orleans when the 520-foot-long Atlantic Asphalt struck it.
Disturbing images showed passengers aboard the cruise line holding on to railings as the ship started to capsize.
The 17,764-dwt vessel that hit the ship typically carries asphalt and was ballasting to Louisiana on Friday, Argus Media reported.
At the time of the collision, the specialized bitumen tanker designed to transport liquid bitumen and other heavy petroleum products at high temperatures, was empty.
Built in 2017, the ship carried the national flag of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, according to Vessel Finder.

text:
«القاهرة» تدعو لتجنب تحميل الدول النامية أعباءً اقتصادية جديدة

Scientists have moved a step closer to diagnosing the degenerative brain condition chronic traumatic encephalopathy in living people, after a study found a blood biomarker that identifies an advanced form of the disease.
As things stand CTE, which is caused by repeated trauma to the head and is especially prevalent in collision and contact sports such as American football, rugby and football, can be diagnosed only after death by examining brain tissue.
However, scientists at Washington University School of Medicine in St Louis have now identified a protein fragment in blood – eMTBR-tau243 – that is elevated not only in Alzheimer’s disease but also in other brain diseases that share the same type of toxic protein buildup, including CTE.
“We are potentially opening a new door for diagnosing and treating CTE in living patients,” said Kanta Horie, the co-senior author of the study in the medical journal JAMA Neurology.

title: Is your child being bullied at school? Warning signs UAE parents should look out for
text:
Not all children who are bullied show physical injuries. Some may become quieter, avoid friends, or suddenly not want to go to school. UAE educators say parents should watch for these signs as Dubai introduces new measures to protect pupils.
Bullying can show up as repeated name-calling, being left out of groups, or hurtful messages on social media. Children often do not tell parents or teachers because they are worried that speaking up will make things worse.
A 2025 survey of 629 UAE students in Grades 6 to 8 found that 73 per cent of those who were bullied had not told anyone. Only 41 per cent knew how to report bullying at school, and 49 per cent did not know whether their school had someone in charge of handling bullying.
These findings show how hard it can be for schools and families to spot bullying and help children who are suffering quietly.

title: Marilyn Monroe’s hidden letters and belongings emerge after six decades
text:
For decades, much of 
Marilyn Monroe
's life has been viewed through photographs, film appearances and the relationships that made headlines. A collection preserved by two of her closest friends is now bringing attention to a less familiar part of her story. وإذا تعرض ابن الريف لضائقة باع أى شىء إلا الأرض، فهو يقبل أن يبيع حيواناته التى يعيش منها، ويصرف من عائدها فى حياته، وقد يبيع جزءاً من بيته القديم، ولكنه أبداً لا يبيع أرضه مهما كان حجم ما يجده من ضائقة، ولا يعايره الآخرون بشىء إلا بأنه باع أرضه أو جزءاً منها.
هذا ميراث قديم جداً، ويشتد رسوخاً فى الريف، وإذا سافر الريفى ثم عاد من غربة طالت أو قصرت، فإنه يفكر أول ما يفكر فى شراء قطعة أرض، ويرى فى ذلك ما يحقق شيئاً فى داخله، ثم يرى فيه ما يرفع من قدره أمام الجميع.

PAKISTAN Railways has become synonymous with the image of a decaying organisation: accident-prone, loss-making and inefficient. Not many are willing to admit that mismanagement, unsteady wagons, rickety tracks and 18th-century mindset have reduced the Railways to a near-death existence.
Even when it reluctantly continues to chug, rattle and rumble, everyone knows that it is managed and operated in a way not much different from a lorry adda across the road. The only option left seems to lie in the old Dakota Indian tribal wisdom: “When you discover that you are riding a dead horse, the best strategy is to dismount.”
Pakistan Railways has simply run out of steam. A meltdown was only natural. title: Over 15,000 flights delayed or canceled in US due to system failure — website

text:
NEW YORK, November 14. /TASS/. The number of delayed or canceled flights in the US due to a system failure has exceeded 15,000, the FlightAware website reported.
According to its information, 8,501 flights within, to, or from the US were delayed and 7,218 flights were canceled.
Earlier, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) suspended departures from all airports nationwide for approximately 4.5 hours due to issues with air traffic control equipment. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said that the outage was caused by outdated equipment, for the replacement of which the US Congress must allocate $50 billion.

title: At Art Mumbai, UAE galleries reflect on historic and contemporary ties between India and the Gulf
text:
Nujoom Alghanem’s Voyage has the uncanny effect of feeling both tempestuous and serene, like looking at a boat on a misty dawn or, conversely, on a cloudless day.
A lot of this is due to the painting’s grit and texture: the dabs and creases of black paint that have been superimposed on the abstracted seascape, the boat with its sailors. Without the black paint, the scene would have plunged into indecipherable abstraction.
It wouldn’t have been a bad painting – if anything, the white figures would have evoked a textual quality – but it would have been a completely different work. The painting would have lost its delightful climatic ambiguity. It would no longer have been a seascape.
At Art Mumbai, Abu Dhabi’s Rizq Art Gallery is highlighting the painting’s maritime imagery. Voyage is one of several works by Alghanem that draw on the UAE’s seafaring traditions.
In Mumbai, this aspect also comes to allude to the city’s historic position as a trading hub between India and the Gulf region.

title: US loses its status of country that eliminated measles — newspaper
summary: According to the newspaper, more than 5,400 cases of measles were reported in the US in 2026, marking the highest number in several decades
text:
NEW YORK, November 14. /TASS/. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has stripped the US of its status as a country where endemic measles transmission has been eliminated, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources.
According to the newspaper, more than 5,400 cases of measles were reported in the US in 2026, marking the highest number in several decades. In November alone, five deaths were recorded in Pennsylvania, New York, and Wisconsin as a result of unrelated outbreaks of the disease.
The US achieved measles-free status in 2000 thanks to large-scale vaccination campaigns. However, the percentage of children attending daycare who are vaccinated against measles, mumps, and rubella has dropped from 95.2% to 92.4% over the past six years.
To regain this status, the US must ensure that there is no sustained transmission of the virus for at least 12 months. According to the newspaper, this could take years.

text:
Weather forecasting in the Southern Hemisphere is challenging. Here's why
It's not easy to forecast the weather in the Southern Hemisphere.
Atmospheric scientists such as Kimberley Reid from the University of Melbourne face a number of unique challenges that make observing weather trickier here than in the Northern Hemisphere.
"The Northern Hemisphere has … so much more land mass. There's more people and more funding for observations, and more major cities," Dr Reid said.
"In the Southern Hemisphere … we don't have as many surface observations, or as many weather balloons, which are all necessary for working out what's going on."
Despite this, in recent years the Southern Hemisphere has narrowed the forecasting gap, with accuracy that almost matches our northern counterparts.

title: The algorithm’s autograph: Can Artificial Intelligence ever become an ‘author’?
summary: Can AI strike the sweet spot between authorial omnipresence and invisibility? What does it even look like?
text:
Writing is a form of artificial intelligence. That is pretty much what Socrates felt about the new technology of transcription, about which he was rather suspicious. Plato’s reconstructed teacher did not actually call it AI, of course. But he described writing in terms that mysteriously evoke the current reality and conversations around machine intelligence.
Writing was, for Plato, an “invention” that “will produce forgetfulness in the minds of those who learn to use it, because they will not practice their memory”. People’s “trust in writing, produced by external characters which are no part of themselves, will discourage the use of their own memory within them”. This is gradually how we come to outsource our own human functions to external technology – a process, in today’s language, called “metacognitive laziness”.

text:

- Published
Days after her 12-year-old son was killed by a BMW driver travelling at 70mph, Louise Slater sat outside the suspect's home, gathering the courage to plead with his family to hand him in.
She had been given the name and address of Aleksanders Dolars after her son Keaton was killed in a hit-and-run in Coventry.
Distraught, she was preparing to knock on the door when a neighbour approached and asked what she was doing.
When she explained, he told her the family, from Latvia, had packed up and left a day or two earlier.
Keaton's suspected killer had fled just hours after leaving him dying in the road.

ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s fiscal buffers weakened in the first quarter of the current fiscal year despite expenditure controls and subsidy cuts, as revenue-to-GDP ratios declined and provincial cash surpluses shrank.
The overall fiscal surplus fell to 0.9 per cent of GDP in July-September this year from 1.7pc a year ago, according to fiscal operations data released by the Ministry of Finance.

title: Microsoft Outlook and Teams outage eases after over a day but recovery timeline uncertain
summary: Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system.
text:
A global outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams was easing after more than 24 hours of disruption crippled online communications across businesses and governments, though the company said it still had no timeline for full recovery of services.
Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system. It said it was not aware of any malicious activity and ruled out AI as the cause.
Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings.
ai_summary: Microsoft is working to restore Outlook and Teams services following a global outage that disrupted business and government communications.

KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to gradually replace conventional vehicles used in government departments with electric vehicles (EVs), in a move aimed at cutting expenditure, saving fuel and reducing pollution.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Austerity, chaired by Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon and attended by Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah.
The meeting reviewed measures to reduce government expenditure, save fuel and assess the vehicle requirements of various departments.
According to a press statement, the meeting decided to purchase vehicles for the home department, the Anti-Corruption Establishment and the universities and boards department, and agreed that electric vehicles would be given preference in future purchases for government departments.

US flights halted nationwide after FAA communications outage
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered a nationwide ground stop following a telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control operations, suspending departures across the country. Flights already airborne have been allowed to continue to their destinations while authorities work to resolve the disruption.
More than 10,000 flights were delayed and over 2,000 cancelled, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware, with CBS News reporting that a software update to a private communications network connecting air traffic control facilities across the US caused the system to reboot and crash, triggering the outage.
The nationwide ground stop is the first since January 2023, when an FAA computer system malfunction disrupted operations. The previous major halt followed the September 11, 2001 attacks.

Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.
Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.
More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.

Rosstandart, Russia’s federal standards agency, has approved a state standard (GOST) titled “Traditional Russian cuisine: Recommendations for preparing dishes” (registered users can view it here). The document includes recipes, preparation methods, and serving suggestions for 132 dishes.
An Industry and Trade Ministry working group developed the standard. Its members included officials and representatives from the restaurant industry. Industry and Trade Minister Anton Alikhanov said the document was “not an attempt to regulate everything, but a guide that guarantees consumers authenticity and high quality.”
“[Today] only 1% of restaurants in the country describe themselves as serving Russian cuisine. In effect, we’ve lost an important part of our cultural identity,” the minister said. He said the standard should “reverse this trend.”

Germany’s parliament has approved a bill significantly expanding the powers of the country’s intelligence agencies. The law aims to counter espionage, terrorism, and sabotage, the newspaper Die Welt reported.
The changes apply to the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) and the Federal Intelligence Service (BND).
The law allows the agencies to:
- Secretly enter homes
- Carry out cyberattacks on foreign IT systems
- Delete or alter data or redirect internet traffic
- Use AI to analyze biometric data
- Recruit teenagers 16 and older as informants in exceptional cases
A special body, including former judges, will review whether proposed measures are legal before the agencies carry them out.
The authorities said the law was needed because of growing hybrid threats from Russia, China, and Iran.

title: Security siren goes off at UK military base for second time today — newspaper
summary: The Feltwell base is located in Norfolk in eastern England
text:
LONDON, November 14. /TASS/. A security siren sounded at RAF Feltwell, used by the US Air Force, amid reports of unidentified drones in the area, The Daily Mail reported, citing eyewitnesses.
A woman interviewed by the newspaper, who lives near the base, said that that at approximately 5:30 p.m. local time (same as GMT) on November 13, she heard "war sirens," which lasted for five minutes. "We thought maybe it was a drill. Then we heard an American male voice from the speakers telling people to remain indoors and shelter," the woman said. The Feltwell base is located in Norfolk in eastern England.
Earlier, Sky News reported, citing a statement from a US Air Force spokesperson, that drones had been detected over the US-operated Royal Air Force Lakenheath in Suffolk, England. Following this, US servicemen were ordered to take shelter. No one was injured as a result of the incident.
The Lakenheath base is located approximately ten kilometers (6.2 miles) from the Feltwell base.

title: SpaceX Starship megarocket blasts off before expected return for reuse
summary: Flight 15 expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over 22 hours, before company catches it at Starbase, Texas SpaceX’s Starship megarocket blasted off from Texas on Friday afternoon, as the aerospace company sought to make history with a double catch of its reusable rocket. Starship Flight 15 is expected to orbit the Earth about 14 times over the course of 22 hours, before the company catches the rocket at its launchpad at Starbase, in south Texas. Continue reading...
text:
SpaceX’s Starship megarocket blasted off from Texas on Friday afternoon, as the aerospace company sought to make history with a double catch of its reusable rocket.
Starship Flight 15 is expected to orbit the Earth about 14 times over the course of 22 hours, before the company catches the rocket at its launchpad at Starbase, in south Texas.
The rocket itself was composed of two elements: the lower booster, with 33 raptor engines that fired off during takeoff, and the Starship at the top.
SpaceX had planned for both components to return to its tower, but the booster, named Super Heavy, was aborted and splashed down in the sea. The cause of that diversion remains unknown.
The Starship continued on sailing through space.
SpaceX has launched a flurry of test flights in recent years, as its chief executive Elon Musk pushes his vision of taking humans into space.
More details soon …
ai_summary: SpaceX launched its Starship megarocket from Texas, successfully testing flight components while experiencing an unexpected abort of the booster stage.

Baby monitor company Owlet shares warning for parents after child's death
Owlet, a popular baby monitor company, is sharing a warning for parents following a child's death.
The company posted a notice on its website and social media pages Friday, saying the company "was recently made aware" that a child died after getting "entangled in a loose and exposed camera cable" that was part of an Owlet camera.
"As fellow parents, our hearts are with this family during this very difficult time," Owlet said in its statement.
It continued, "Although the provided camera cable guards were not in use at the time of this particular event, we've reviewed our records and are currently aware of 91 adhesive-related complaints. title: Nvidia crisis spurs scrutiny of agency that oversees chip curbs
summary: Congress is demanding answers about whether the Bureau of Industry and Security did enough to keep Nvidia's AI processors out of China's hands.
text:
The Trump administration official who runs U.S. export control programs was looking for marquee names for his agency’s upcoming annual conference and threw an unusual option into the mix: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler had expressed interest in recent months in inviting Huang to be a speaker at the Bureau of Industry and Security event on Jan. 10 in Washington, according to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified discussing private deliberations.
Kessler bragged about his ability to get Huang to attend, the people said, though the then-Nvidia chief ultimately fell out of the running. A BIS spokesperson said no speakers have been invited to the conference yet and planning is still under way.
ai_summary: US officials previously considered inviting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to a government conference on export controls before his recent departure from the company.

title: Nvidia approaches Arm CEO Haas as employees seek Huang’s return, reports say
summary: Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role and had not formally engaged any potential candidates.
text:
Nvidia’s board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times said on Friday, even as another report said some employees were pushing to bring back the former CEO.
Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shock waves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.
Haas’ name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang’s exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013.
ai_summary: Nvidia's board is considering Arm CEO Rene Haas as a successor to Jensen Huang following Huang's resignation amid a corporate scandal.

title: Texas brothers convicted in $240 million cattle investment fraud targeting 2,200 investors
summary: Convicted of a fraudulent cattle investment scheme, Joshua and Jason Link swindled over 2,200 investors, misleading them into thinking their money was turning into cattle purchases. Their actions resulted in colossal financial damages, as they raised more than $240 million through non-existent contracts. Investigations uncovered that funds were misused for personal luxuries rather than fulfilling their financial promises to investors.
text:
What seemed like a chance to invest in cattle and profit from the meat business turned into a multimillion-dollar fraud that hit thousands of Americans. Investors were led to believe their money would buy, raise and process cattle until the meat could be sold at a profit. But federal prosecutors say the business operated on a very different model, using money from new investors to pay earlier commitments and fund personal luxuries. The scheme has now led to the federal conviction of two brothers in Texas.

في عام 1824وبقرية برنبال الجديدة بمركز دكرنس بمحافظة الدقهلية وفي عام 1824 ولد علي مبارك والذي يطلق عليه المؤرخون لقب أبوالتعليم، وقد تلقى تعليمه الأساسى بكتّاب القرية وحفظ القرآن، وتعلم مبادئ القراءة والكتابة وأدى تفوقه في التعليم الابتدائى إلى اختياره للتعلم بمدرسة قصرالعينى التجهيزية، ثم انتقل للمدرسة التجهيزية في«أبوزعبل» لثلاث سنوات وفى عام 1839 اختير مع مجموعة من المتفوقين للالتحاق بمدرسة المهندسخانة في بولاق لخمس سنوات، ودرس الجبر والهندسة والطبيعة والكيمياء والمعادن والجيولوجيا والفلك، ومساحة الأراضي والطبوغرافيا.

title: No radar outage: National Weather Service sets record straight
summary: No radar outage: National Weather Service sets record straight News4JAX US National Weather Service says its radars operating normally Reuters National Weather Service hit by internet outages, limiting access to weather updates KRXI2 National Weather Service reports nationwide internet, communications issues Democrat and Chronicle ‘Not true’: National Weather Service says tech issues regional, not widespread WBTV
text:
No radar outage: National Weather Service sets record straight
The National Weather Service is pushing back on misinformation circulating online about a radar outage.
According to the NWS, radar.weather.gov is fully operational and no outage exists. The agency says outdated content from isolated webpages has been spreading, leading some to believe the radar network is down.
“In case you heard otherwise, there is no radar outage and radar.weather.gov is fully operational,” the NWS posted. “Outdated content from isolated webpages stating otherwise has been circulating, but NWS radars are operating normally.”
News4JAX reached out to the National Weather Service Jacksonville, which told us everything is operational and the rumor is false.

text:
Six Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza
Israeli attacks killed six Palestinians and injured around 20 others across the Gaza Strip on Friday, according to medical sources and witnesses.
In Deir al-Balah, a double-tap strike hit civilians who were helping victims of an earlier attack, witnesses said.
Israeli artillery shelled the area around the al-Qastal Towers residential complex, east of the city, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. Those wounded were taken to al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah.
Israeli artillery also shelled eastern areas of Gaza City, Wafa added.
Since the ceasefire took effect on 11 October 2025, Israeli attacks have killed 1,622 Palestinians and injured 5,878 others, according to Gaza's health ministry.

text:
Europe taps national security advisers to represent the continent in Russia-Ukraine peace talks
National security advisers from the European Union, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy, and Poland will represent Europe in upcoming talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war, Bloomberg reported.
European leaders made the decision after a summit in Dublin on November 12 and 13.
European Council President António Costa and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed the makeup of the European delegation.
“Our principles and our positions in these negotiations remain well known.
“And our European team will continue to act in full unity and in close coordination with all member states,” Costa wrote on X.
A senior European official told Bloomberg that the advisers would take part in the upcoming talks at the technical level. Europe has yet to appoint representatives for negotiations at the highest level.

text:
Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
US President Donald Trump has extended by 90 days a waiver of a shipping law so that foreign-flagged ships can transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.
The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources.
The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched its war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices.
When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension.
The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war.

text:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop for all flights that are due to take off in the US on Friday, delaying or canceling nearly 7,000 US flights, according to aviation tracker FlightAware.
In a post on X, the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said the stoppage is due to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” and that the FAA’s technicians are looking into the matter.
This is the third time all departing flights have been grounded in the US. The first time was on 11 September 2001; the other was in January 2023, when the FAA paused all domestic departures for less than two hours after a pilot notification system malfunctioned.
The FAA has more than 14,000 air traffic controllers who handle the more than 44,000 flights that take off from airports across the US each day, according to FAA data.

Tasmania, as entomologist Peter McQuillan puts it, is "a Noah's Ark of ancient species long since lost elsewhere".
One of those living relics is the pandani moth.
The bronze-brown insect is large for its species, with big legs and a purplish reflective hue under light.
It has also lost the ability to fly, moving about mostly by hopping — although it can glide down from the Tasmanian pandani, a slow growing alpine plant that the moth lives in.
It was first seen in the 1980s, given a formal name by Dr McQuillan in the early 2000s and then rarely seen — until last year, when a group of volunteers from Wildcare Tasmania surveyed the population in the state's remote south-west.
The group call themselves the Friends of the Pandani Moth.

The union, whose members work across probation offices and in family courts, said it launched its ballot because of an “inadequate” 5% pay offer from ministers and a failure to cut workloads.
Probation officers have come under increasing pressure since the launch of the latest early release scheme in October, which is meant to ease overcrowding in prisons.

text:
GOP firebrand Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., is projected to lose her seat in the House to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher.
The Associated Press made the call in the razor-thin race Friday afternoon in favor of Laubacher, who maintained her slim 48.7% lead over Boebert’s 47.9% once 99% of the ballots had been counted.
Libertarian candidate Douglas Mangeris came in third with a little more than 3% of the vote.
Lubacher is projected to win Colorado’s 4th Congressional District, according to the AP.
Boebert was running for her fourth term in the state. She served her first two seats in Colorado’s third district, and was running for her second term in the state’s fourth district.
The 39-year-old congresswoman’s loss comes amid a blue wave that saw Democrats flip seats in Republican strongholds like Texas, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.
Democrats now have 256 seats in the House of Representatives to Republicans’ 169. A party needs 218 for a majority.

title: 'That’s what they deserve' — Zakharova about TASS’ expulsion from EANA
summary: Earlier on Friday, the EANA General Assembly expelled TASS, whose membership was suspended back in March 2022
text:
MOSCOW, November 13. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova has commented on TASS's expulsion from the European Alliance of News Agencies (EANA) by saying that Europe "deserves" it.
Earlier on Friday, the EANA General Assembly expelled TASS, whose membership was suspended back in March 2022. At the same time, the alliance voted to admit Lithuania’s news agency ELTA.
"That’s what they deserve," Zakharova told TASS.
Founded at the Conference on New Media Technology in Strasbourg in 1956, EANA is an alliance of European news agencies uniting one leading agency from each European country. Its supreme decision-making body is its General Assembly, which meets once a year. The alliance also holds conferences twice a year, with the second one being held jointly with the General Assembly.
After expelling TASS and admitting Lithuania’s ELTA, EANA continues to have 33 members.
ai_summary: Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova commented on the expulsion of TASS from the European Alliance of News Agencies.

SpaceX will attempt to catch both parts of its huge Starship rocket after it launches on its next test flight on Friday.
Elon Musk's company will use the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower to grab the rocket parts mid-air as they return to Earth.

Nasa will be closely watching the flight: the SpaceX rocket is set to play a vital part in its Artemis programme, which will see astronauts land on the Moon.

text:
Trump to rule on tariffs for Australian lamb after US trade commissioners disagree
A US trade panel reviewing Australian lamb imports into the United States has been unable to agree on whether the American industry has been hurt by the imports.
The rare tie-vote at the US International Trade Commission (USITC) means US President Donald Trump will ultimately decide whether to place tariffs or other trade restrictions on the Australian meat.
"A tie vote … means the president can decide which vote (affirmative or negative) he chooses the 'winning' vote," Georgetown University's Jennifer Hillman, a former USITC commissioner, told the ABC.
"[I] would presume, particularly in light of the plight of farmers in the US generally, that he would be inclined to treat this as an affirmative determination and impose tariffs or tariff rate quotas."
The next step in the process is a public "remedies" hearing to debate those measures before commissioners make final recommendations to the White House.

Some of the most enduring theories of power were born in its absence. text:
MOSCOW, November 13. /TASS/. TASS has been expelled from the European Alliance of News Agencies (EANA) without any notification or explanation, the alliance said on its website following a secret ballot by its General Assembly.
In February 2022, the alliance’s governing body, the EANA Council, informed TASS that it was suspending the agency’s membership. The reason it cited was that, due to restrictions imposed by Russia’s telecom watchdog Roskomnadzor, TASS "is acting contrary to the EANA’s mission, namely, it can no longer serve as a provider of unbiased news."
The issue of expelling TASS was raised during the EANA assemblies in 2022 and 2023, but at those times, the expulsion didn't garner enough votes to pass. A decision was made to suspend TASS’s membership in the alliance without formally expelling it.

ai_summary: The European Alliance of News Agencies has expelled the Russian news agency TASS following a secret ballot.

CCTV footage shows the moment a bus approaches a stop with two riders waiting with their horses. After a discussion with the driver, the riders walk the horses onto the bus briefly before de-boarding.
The City of Detroit said its Department of Transportation allows service animals on buses in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. But officials say that in this event, the horses appeared to have been brought on board for unrelated reasons, creating safety concerns for other passengers and for the horses themselves.
The city said it would now provide additional training for bus drivers.
One of the riders later told local media that he brought the horses on board to raise awareness of black cowboys and urban equestrian culture.

text:
During NATO’s formative years, the U.S. military commitment to the old continent was a tenuous thing. Dwight Eisenhower, appointed the first supreme allied commander of Europe in 1950, argued—amid a vicious debate in Washington over committing additional divisions to Europe—that American forces should only act as a bridge until Europe stepped up to defend itself. If the United States still had troops in Europe 10 years hence, he said in 1951, then the trans-Atlantic project would be a failure.
Ike’s forecast, it seems, was wrong on both counts. Seventy-five years on, roughly 80,000 U.S. troops remain on the continent. Yet few would regard the alliance as a failure. The U.S. military commitment succeeded in guaranteeing Europe’s freedom and keeping the Soviets at bay. But Europe never fully shouldered the burden of its own defense.

In 1850, drought had ravaged the lands now known as Victoria.
"The country from the Murray to the sea was brown with desiccated herbage, and forests charged with resinous matter baked to the verge of conflagration," Henry Gyles Turner wrote in History of the Colony of Victoria.
"It wanted but some slightly careless act of man to set in motion a devastating fury against which no human intervention could stand."
That "devastating fury" arrived on February 6, 1851.
As temperatures soared into the 40s across the state, fires took hold of what was then the Port Phillip colony.
Five million hectares of land burned from the Wimmera, south to Mount Gambier and Portland, across to Port Fairy, Geelong and Barwon Heads and through the Macedon, Plenty and Dandenong Ranges around Melbourne's north and east.

Flight BA431 suffered a double tail strike, when the rear of an aircraft scrapes along the runway surface, on Thursday as it attempted to land following a flight from Amsterdam.
New footage has emerged showing the Airbus A321 Neo approaching the runway of Heathrow's Terminal 5 at around 10.30am.
The aircraft appears to sway from side to side before its left wheel touches down on the runway.
After the right wheel makes contact, the plane's tail scrapes along the tarmac in what is known as a double tail strike.
It then takes off again, with pilots performing a so-called go-around, as it leant slightly to the left.
The aircraft was forced to attempt the landing again, eventually landing at 10.49am.

WASHINGTON, Nov 13 - The US Supreme Court agreed on Friday to consider the legality of President Donald Trump's restrictions on access to asylum at the US-Mexico border, a hardline immigration policy his administration has credited with helping reduce border crossings.
The justices took up Trump's appeal of a lower court's ruling that found he exceeded his authority by denying migrants caught entering the country illegally the chance to apply for asylum.
The court is expected to hear arguments in the case in the coming months and rule by the end of June.
Trump, who has described the influx of migrants as an invasion, announced the new curbs just hours into his second presidential term on January 20, 2025. title: What could El Niño mean for winter weather in the US and Canada?
summary: El Niño winters typically bring more rain in the southern USA and drier, warmer conditions further north but the impacts on snowfall are complex.
text:
What could El NiÃ±o mean for winter weather in the US and Canada?
- Published
The developing El NiÃ±o - already the strongest on record by some measures - continues to grow and could have profound effects on the weather across North America this autumn and winter.
The naturally-occurring climate phenomenon sees trade winds over the Pacific Ocean, which usually blow from east to west, weakening or reversing with warm water instead spreading eastwards.
This releases heat into the atmosphere which can drive major shifts in global weather patterns.
Impacts in the US and Canada are varied, with a greater chance of a warm and dry winter in northern areas and more risk of flooding rain further south.
There is also some evidence that El NiÃ±o can increase the likelihood of disruption to the stratospheric polar vortex which can, in turn, bring snowfall later in winter.
No two El NiÃ±os are the same and the impacts are not guaranteed - the odds are just shifted in favour of certain outcomes.

text:
Russian strikes kill one in Zaporizhzhia, two in Odesa
Nov 13 - Russian forces launched strikes on two Ukrainian cities on Friday, killing one person and injuring more than 50 in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia and killing two more in the Black Sea port of Odesa, regional officials said.
In Zaporizhzhia, a five-storey apartment building was hit and seriously damaged. Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram that a rescue worker was killed when a concrete slab collapsed during operations to clear rubble.
Semikin said six children were among the injured.
In Odesa, the head of the city's military administration, Serhiy Lysak said two people died in an attack on a private residence. Five people were injured, including two in a serious condition.
Reuters could not independently confirm the accounts.
Both Ukraine and Russia deny targeting civilians in the 4-1/2-year-old war. REUTERS

The works, which were donated to the gallery by Beckett's sister Hilda Mangan in 1972, had been stored in boxes for years and, because of the materials Beckett favoured, were weathered and cracked, the paint peeling.

title: Boy Found Alive After Search: Roman Heilman found alive; horseback riders spot him
summary: A community came together in a remarkable rescue of six-year-old Roman Heilman, who had been missing for nearly 44 hours in the woods of Kentucky. He was awake and responsive upon rescue and has since been taken to a hospital to address dehydration from his ordeal.
text:
A massive search involving hundreds of volunteers, emergency responders and horseback riders came to a remarkable end in eastern Kentucky after a six-year-old boy with 
autism
, who had been missing for nearly 44 hours, was found alive in the woods. Roman Heilman had spent two nights outdoors in difficult weather before emerging from the thick brush alongside a small dog. His rescue brought relief to a community that had spent days searching the rugged terrain for him. It is a language phenomenon reflective of the UAE’s ambition to become a global hub, the result of a relatively open immigration policy enabling a highly diverse, transient population.
This multilingualism is rightly celebrated, and there is no doubt that the adoption of English has been central to the UAE's growth. But in practice, this widespread acceptance of English has also posed a challenge to the country's native language, and with it the cultural vitality of Arab youths and families living here. A truly multilingual UAE is still feasible, but only if Arabic is treated as indispensable.

ai_summary: The UAE's rapid growth and multilingual environment pose a challenge to the preservation of the Arabic language as the country's official tongue.

title: Iraq's first Jewish Museum opens a door to the past – and a contentious debate on the present
text:
Inside the Shamash Jewish Museum in Baghdad, the elegant glass-fronted wooden display cases hold a paper trail to a vanished Iraq.
Some of the neatly arranged documents are originals, yellowed and fraying at the edges, while others are carefully reproduced copies. Together, they reconstruct the daily life of Iraqi Jews: school certificates, handwritten letters, identity cards, marriage contracts, family photographs of children in uniforms and shopkeepers in their stores.
On the walls hang framed black-and-white portraits, including of Sassoon Heskel (1860–1932), an Iraqi-Jewish statesman and the first minister of finance of the Kingdom of Iraq, and a brass seven-branched candelabrum.
A message on one shelf states that the museum offers an opportunity to “rediscover an important part of Iraq's diverse cultural and religious heritage,” while helping to “preserve its memory for future generations.”
Set up in the former Shamash Jewish School founded in 1928 by Jewish philanthropist Yacoub
ai_summary: The newly opened Shamash Jewish Museum in Baghdad aims to preserve the history and cultural heritage of Iraq's Jewish community.

title: As GTA VI arrives, how 40 years of gaming helped me navigate love, fatherhood and loss
text:
I had just named my planet Bragi when I got the call. It was Lewisham Hospital in south London. They suggested I come quickly. I paused my game and looked at my wife. “It’s Mum,” I said. It was four days before Christmas in 2018 and outside south London was suffering a torrential downpour.
I couldn’t drive because I’d broken my ankle the week before, and so I sat in the back of the car as my wife sped us through the rain-slicked streets of Wimbledon and Tooting, the Christmas lights streaking down the windows as revellers spilt out of pubs.
We were too late. By the time we arrived, she was gone – at 69, no age. What a life, though. Four hours later, we were home. The next week was a fug of unreality, trying to make Christmas fun for the kids while figuring out how to live without “silly old Grandma”. New Year rolled around, and with it, the return of school and routine. That’s when the work really started.
I decided to return to Bragi.

Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.
Haas’ name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang’s exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013.
He is among several candidates being considered, and there is no guarantee he will be offered the job or accept it, the FT reported. Nvidia’s finance chief Colette Kress is the interim CEO.
Arm declined to comment, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.
